A1.reason: split_work_to_cores(row_wise=True) is applied, but on a 130-core grid the op uses 128 cores, so row-wise and column-wise select almost the same set and the DRAM-facing spread is identical. Delta is inside noise on every bench shape (grid_filling -0.6%, row_major -0.9%, smallest -1.4%). Kept on: it costs nothing and it is the right default the moment the op runs on a partial grid.

A2.reason: Launch only on cores that hold data requires a sharded input; Phase 0 SUPPORTED[memory_layout] is INTERLEAVED only, so there are no shard-owning cores to launch on.
A2.followup: Lamp L3: add HEIGHT_SHARDED, back cb_input_tiles with ttnn.cb_descriptor_from_sharded_tensor and set CORE_GRID from the shard grid.

A3.reason: Interleaved pages are spread over every DRAM bank by the TensorAccessor, so a core cannot be made adjacent to 'its' bank; only the A1 axis spread is expressible. A3 becomes real once the input is sharded (each core then owns one bank's worth of rows).
A3.followup: With Lamp L3 sharding, map each shard to its NoC-optimal worker (get_optimal_worker_cores_for_sharded_tensor).

A4.reason: The remainder is handled by split_work_to_cores' two core groups and by padding the final row-block to a full BLOCK_HT (phantom tile-rows clamped to the last valid one), so no core is idle - but there is no specialised cliff kernel, and the cliff core still pays for BLOCK_HT tile-rows of work when it owns fewer.
A4.followup: Emit a second kernel variant for the cliff core with its own BLOCK_HT; measure on a shape whose Rt is coprime with the grid (e.g. (1,1,3232,96), Rt=101).

B0.reason: Every per-core-overhead lever's counterfactual was measured on the smallest regime the op accepts, (32,17) = 1 tile of real work: A0 -1.1%, A1 -1.4%, B5 -1.7%, B7 +0.3%, B9 -0.2%, C16 -1.2%, compute_block_size -1.6%. Nothing regresses that regime beyond +-1.7% (noise), so no lever needs a work-per-core gate in Phase 0.

B5.reason: Every transfer is a whole tile page (noc_async_read_tile / noc_async_write_tile); the RM path moves whole padded sticks. Splitting each 2048 B tile into two 1024 B halves costs +9.1% on (1,1,8192,1024) and +10.1% on (1,1,32,7168); no regression on (32,17) (-1.7%, noise).

B6.reason: The one-packet fast path needs transfers <= 512 B; a bf16 tile page is 2048 B (fp32 4096 B). Reaching it means giving up B5's coalescing, and the same `coalesce` knob measures exactly that direction: halving to 1024 B - still above 512 B - already costs +9.1%. Shrinking further to 512 B goes further the wrong way, so the fast path is not reachable at a profit for this op's page size.

B7.reason: One noc_async_read_barrier / noc_async_write_barrier per BLOCK (BLOCK_HT x chunk_wt tiles, or one tile-row of sticks on the RM path) instead of per transaction. Largest single dataflow lever on this op: 1.33x on (1,1,8192,1024), 1.32x on the RM path, and 3.56x on the single-core wide-decode shape (1,1,32,7168) where there is nothing else to hide latency behind.

B8.reason: Reads are already issued as a whole block before one barrier (B7), so within a block requests are in flight; trid double-issue would additionally overlap ACROSS blocks. The grid-filling shape runs 1 row-block per core, so there is no next block to overlap against - the bench cannot show it there. wide_prefill (2 blocks/core) and (99991,64) (28 blocks/core) could.
B8.followup: Add a trid arm (noc_async_read_tile_with_trid + barrier on the previous id) and measure on wide_prefill and (99991,64), where blocks-per-core > 1.

B9.reason: Reader on NoC0 (ReaderConfigDescriptor) and writer on NoC1 (WriterConfigDescriptor). This op reads and writes a full tensor, so the two streams are the same size; forcing both onto NOC_0 costs 1.47x on (1,1,8192,1024) and 1.47x on the RM path. Flat on the 1-core wide-decode shape (the streams are serialised by the 2-pass structure there) and on (32,17).

B10.reason: Per-reader virtual-channel assignment is only meaningful once several readers share a route; with 128 cores each reading interleaved pages from all banks the routes are already spread, and B9 already removed the read/write contention that dominates.
B10.followup: Add a `vc` arm on the reader's noc_async_read and measure on (1,1,8192,1024) after Lamp L2 removes the gamma re-reads (which currently hide small routing effects).

B11.reason: Every DRAM address this op forms is alignment-legal by construction: tile transfers go through TensorAccessor's aligned page stride, and the two byte-offset paths (RM stick W-chunk, RM gamma slice) use offsets that are multiples of 32*element_size (>= 64 B). There is no misaligned variant to measure - one is a hardware fault, not a slower arm. The acceptance suite run under --dev (NoC sanitizer on) is the mechanical pin: it caught exactly this class of bug when an earlier gamma path issued a read at stick offset +32 B on a 64 B-aligned device.

B12.regime: Prefill on a full grid, where rows-per-core is small: (1,1,8192,1024) puts Rt=256 row-blocks on 128 cores, so all 128 cores re-read the same Wt=32 gamma tiles from DRAM. Measured upper bound on the headroom: with gamma 93981 ns vs no gamma at all 89030 ns = 5.3%, and that difference also contains the second `mul`, so the pure re-read cost is below 5.3%. The design's byte model predicted 21% - the measurement says the replication is largely absorbed, which is why this is recorded as small-but-real rather than scheduled ahead of Lamp L1.
B12.reason: Lamp L2: read gamma once on an injector core and mcast it (mcast_pipe SenderPipe/ReceiverPipe) instead of num_cores DRAM re-reads. cb_gamma_tiles is already a resident, never-popped CB filled exactly once per core, so switching its fill from TensorAccessor to ReceiverPipe is a reader-local change.

B13.reason: set_state/with_state amortises command-buffer setup over many same-shape transfers to varying addresses - which is exactly this op's inner loop (nw same-size tile reads per block).
B13.followup: Add a `stateful` arm using noc_async_read_tile_with_state and measure on (1,1,8192,1024) and on (32,17) (B0: it adds fixed per-core setup).

C14.reason: Zero-copy aliasing of a CB onto a shard buffer requires a sharded input; Phase 0 is interleaved-only.
C14.followup: Lamp L3: ttnn.cb_descriptor_from_sharded_tensor(CB_INPUT_TILES, input_tensor) once HEIGHT_SHARDED is in SUPPORTED - no NoC read at all for the resident rows.

C15.reason: Same gate as C14/A2: the op is DRAM-interleaved in Phase 0, so it cannot take the L1-resident path. The measured ablation says this is where the money is on the prefill shapes - stubbing the NoC payload on (1,1,8192,1024) drops the op to 26% of its full time.
C15.followup: Lamp L3 (HEIGHT_SHARDED) then Lamp L1 (WIDTH/BLOCK_SHARDED with the cross-core combine).

C16.reason: Applied and live: the budget solver reaches IN_BUF_DEPTH=4, OUT/RM depth 2 on the grid-filling shape (forcing 1/1/1 is a genuinely different plan, verified). It measures flat anyway (+0.1% on grid_filling, -0.7% on the RM path, 0.0% on grid_starved) because those shapes are already DRAM-saturated at ~358 GB/s of useful traffic - deepening the CB cannot create bandwidth. KEPT at its working default: it costs nothing here and it is the lever that pays once the op stops being DM-bound (Lamp L1/L3 move the wall).

C17.reason: rms_norm is not an in-place op on its public contract - it allocates a fresh output tensor. Writing into the input buffer would need a caller opt-in, and the input is still being read in pass B of Regime B.
C17.followup: Add an `output_tensor=` parameter so a caller can alias, and gate it on Regime A (single-read) where the input is fully consumed before the scale pass writes.

D18.reason: Already in the applied FORM - every TensorAccessorArgs is emitted through get_compile_time_args() and read back with TensorAccessorArgs<N>() in the kernels, so address generation is unrolled per buffer type. What is missing is the counterfactual arm that would close it with a number.
D18.followup: Add a `runtime_accessor_args` arm that passes the accessor args as runtime args and measure on (1,1,8192,1024) and (32,17).

D19.reason: Already in the applied FORM - the only runtime args are buffer base addresses plus the per-core (start_row_block, num_row_blocks) pair and the two fp32 scalar bit patterns; every geometry constant is a compile-time arg. No counterfactual arm yet.
D19.followup: Add an arm that demotes the geometry prefix to runtime args and measure the program-cache re-dispatch cost.

D20.reason: The op already selects between two structurally different plans by a pinned host predicate (Regime A resident vs Regime B streaming) and between the TILE and ROW_MAJOR data paths at compile time - which is layout/special-case factory selection. Not closed with a number because forcing the wrong regime is a correctness change, not just a slower arm.
D20.followup: Add a `force_regime` arm that runs Regime B on a shape that fits Regime A, so the single-read fast path can be priced. Predicted from the byte model: Regime B moves 1.5x the DRAM bytes.

D21.reason: Per-core indexing IS precomputed host-side (start_row_block / num_row_blocks per core); the kernels only add. The InterleavedAddrGenFast half does not apply - TensorAccessor is mandatory and already specialises its address generation at compile time.
D21.followup: Add an arm that computes the per-core row range in-kernel from a core index, to price the host-side precompute.

E22.reason: Metal Trace + multiple command queues is a whole-model lever; this is a single-op deliverable and the measurement here is on-device kernel duration, which host-dispatch overlap does not change.
E22.followup: Out of single-op scope; revisit when rms_norm is benched inside a model.

F23.reason: The op cannot downgrade a caller-supplied precision knob: after validate(), the caller's ComputeConfigDescriptor is handed to the compute KernelDescriptor verbatim (config=cfg) and is never rebuilt or mutated. The only value the op chooses is its own default, and that lives in the single exported default_compute_kernel_config() factory. The named test passes an explicit descriptor and asserts the result; test_rms_norm_default_compute_kernel_config_is_a_factory pins the factory itself.

F24.reason: bfp8_pack_precise selects how the packer writes a bfloat8_b tile. This op never emits one: SUPPORTED[dtype] is {float32, bfloat16} and the output dtype is always the input dtype, so there is no bfloat8_b pack for the knob to govern. The golden suite is the mechanical pin - every bfloat8_b cell is xfail-strict there and the suite passes.

F25.reason: fp32_dest_acc_en is a GATED axis pinned to True for Phase 0 by the prompt and by references/precision_convention.md, and every measured cell supplies it explicitly - so F23's boundary applies and the op must not downgrade it. The cost is real and already visible indirectly: DEST_AUTO_LIMIT is 4 instead of 8, which halves the DEST_BLOCK the compute_block_size lever runs at (that lever is worth 1.035x-1.06x today at DEST_BLOCK=4).
F25.followup: The refinement that adds {bfloat16, fp32_dest_acc_en=False} to SUPPORTED: DEST doubles 4->8, so DEST_BLOCK doubles and B5/B7/C16/compute_block_size must all be re-swept at the new block factor. Measure with the existing `dest_block` bench knob once the axis is supported.

F26.reason: master.md's own structural closure: a lossless unpack path buys nothing downstream of any FPU phase. Every path in this op hits at least one - sum_of_squares and the scale multiplies are FPU binaries, reduce<SUM, REDUCE_ROW> is FPU/GMPOOL, and the RM path's tilize uses the fast (fp32->tf32) route by design. So the fp32->TF32 drop happens regardless and Fp32Mode::Lossless / UnpackToDestFp32 would only buy the slower unpack. The named float32 test passes at PCC 0.999 on the default (fast) path, so the precision the lever would protect is not needed.

F27.regime: Compute-bound shapes where the CALLER leaves math_fidelity unset, so the op's own default applies. Measured ladder on (1,1,32,7168) (the ablation says that shape is compute-dominated: stubbing compute drops it to 41% of full): HiFi4 76114 ns, HiFi2 52430 ns (1.45x), LoFi 50293 ns (1.51x). On the DM-bound prefill shape (1,1,8192,1024) the same ladder is worth only 1.027x (93236 -> 90799), exactly as the bound classification predicts.
F27.reason: NOT changed in Phase 0. references/precision_convention.md and the op prompt pin the exported default_compute_kernel_config() to HiFi4, and F23 forbids downgrading a caller-supplied value - every golden cell and every perf loose case supplies math_fidelity explicitly (the perf cases already pin HiFi2). Recorded with the measured number so the refinement that revisits the op's own default starts from evidence rather than from a guess.
